set.pl: Bear River reach south of Petoskey (1913 gravel pit, not yet placed). Wegemer gravel pit (1913): Franz Z. Wegemer's pit on the bank of Bear River, S of the city.

tw-mi-petoskey-bear-river-ottawa-gold.st: The Detroit Free Press (26 Oct 1913) puts the treasure 'in the immediate vicinity of the present Wegemer gravel pit'; all but one of the Ottawas were killed and he died before explaining; the hermit 'Isaac' dug daily for several years.
src: Detroit Free Press, 26 Oct 1913, p. 69 'Tale of Indian Wealth Hidden Two Centuries Ago…' (Newspapers.com 1048447322)

set.tovw: 1927 wire retelling; no property named; legend
set.st: 1927 wire story (Sturgis dateline): James Strang sent two messengers south from Beaver Island with $126,000 in gold to buy colony land near Sturgis; they did not buy and left 'the money buried on one of the various pieces of property they had viewed'. After Strang's death two counsellors returned with a little lead box holding Joseph Smith's 'spectacles' and books, supposedly buried with the money; their memorandum of the spot 'was lost and with it the treasure'. No farm named. Pin is the town, not a spot.

src: Coldwater Daily Reporter, 10 Dec 1927, p. 6 (Newspapers.com 1370365067; same wire Grand Haven Tribune 10 Dec p. 1, 1133765579)
